{
"score_team_1": 2,
"score_team_2": 1,
"team1_win_probability": 65,
"draw_probability": 20,
"team2_win_probability": 15,

"white_hat": "Objective facts: Argentina are among the world elite, recent World Cup winners (2022) and typically occupy top positions in FIFA rankings; they possess depth in attack and midfield with many players in top European clubs. Austria are a strong European side with organized tactics, several players from top leagues, and have improved international results, but historically less World Cup pedigree and lower overall depth.",
"red_hat": "Intuition and emotion favor Argentina. There is often belief and momentum around their national team in big tournaments; supporters and players carry confidence. Austria inspires respect as a disciplined underdog, and emotionally they can be daring and compact. My gut sense is that Argentina’s flair and winning mentality will edge this tie, but Austria’s discipline could make it tight and nervy.",
"black_hat": "Risks and uncertainties include injuries to key players, squad fatigue, or managerial tinkering that unsettles Argentina. Argentina’s aging core may be less explosive and can be exposed on counters or set-pieces. Austria’s weaknesses are fewer but include limited chance creation against top defenses; yet one clinical counterattack, refereeing decisions, or VAR controversies could overturn expectations and make the forecast wrong.",
"yellow_hat": "Positive factors supporting the prediction: Argentina’s attacking creativity and high-quality finishing often produce goals even against organized defenses; superior depth allows tactical adjustments. Austria’s strengths—compact defense and pressing—also create opportunities on transitions and set-pieces, but the window for scoring is smaller. Overall Argentina has the offensive tools and match-winner experience to secure a narrow victory in regular time.",
"green_hat": "Creative scenarios that could alter the match: an early red card for either side changing tactical shape, a young Argentine substitute bursts onto the stage with a decisive goal, or Austria switches to ultra-compact low block and wins via a late set-piece. Weather, an unusual pitch condition, or a surprise tactical formation (three at the back or strikerless) could favor the underdog and flip probabilities considerably.",
"blue_hat": "Synthesis and final judgment: combining hats, the white hat establishes Argentina as the statistical favorite with deeper squad quality; the red hat increases confidence in an Argentine edge; the black hat introduces meaningful downside risk (injury, overconfidence, single-event variance) reducing certainty; the yellow hat reinforces Argentina’s scoring advantage; the green hat adds low-probability high-impact scenarios. Balancing these, I assign a strong but not overwhelming edge to Argentina (65%), a moderate draw chance (20%) reflecting Austria’s defensive solidity and variance, and a smaller upset probability for Austria (15%). The projected score 2-1 reflects Argentina’s superior attack tempered by Austria’s discipline and set-piece threat, producing a narrow Argentine win." 
}
